summary: Bal Gangadhar Tilak (1856–1920) was an Indologist and historian. He studied at Elphinstone College, Deccan College (B.A., 1877), and Government Law College, Mumbai (LL.B., 1879). He later taught at New English School (~1880–1885) and Fergusson College (~1885–1890).

Bal Krishen Thapar (1921–1995) was an archaeologist and Indologist. He studied at the University of the Punjab, the Institute of Archaeology in Taxila under Mortimer Wheeler, and Heidelberg University. He served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1978–1981).
Bala Sahai Shastri was an Indologist. He served at Panjab University as an Assistant (attested 1932) and later as in-charge of the Sanskrit Section (attested 1941).

Baliram Shukla is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He held positions at Savitribai Phule Pune University, including Head of the Department of Philosophy (attested 2001) and Professor (attested 2026).
Balram Shukla (born 1982) is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Delhi from circa 2003 to 2010 and became a professor there around 2013.

Bangwei Wang (born 1950) is an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and sinologist. After completing his doctoral dissertation at Peking University in 1987, he held professorships there, serving as Professor of Indian and Buddhist Studies (attested 2017) and Boya Retired Professor (attested 2026).

Banikanta Kakati (1894–1952) was a linguist and scholar of religion and Indology. Educated at Cotton University, Presidency University, and the University of Calcutta, he was a professor at Cotton University (1918–1947) and later Dean and Assamese department head at Gauhati University (1948).

Bapu Deva Sastri (1821–1900) was an Indologist who studied at Sehore Sanskrit School and under Lancelot Wilkinson, Dhundhiraja Misra, and Sevarama. He taught at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University from 1842 to 1889.

Barbara A. Holdrege works in religious studies and Indology. She has held posts at the University of California, Santa Barbara, including Associate Professor of the Comparative History of Religions (attested 2000) and Professor (attested 2026).

Barbara E. Ward (1919–1983) was a sinologist educated at Newnham College, the University of London, and the LSE. She held teaching posts at the University of London and the University of Cambridge, as well as visiting professorships at Cornell and CUHK.

Barbara Gerke is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Charles Ramble and Geoffrey Samuel, later working at Humboldt University of Berlin (2011–2015), Oxford (attested 2017), and the University of Vienna (attested 2026).

Barbara Harriss-White (born 1946) is a development studies scholar in Indology. Educated at Newstead Wood School, she held posts at the University of East Anglia (1975–1979), Queen Elizabeth House (~1987–2011), Wolfson College, and the University of Oxford (~1987–2011).

Barbara Mittler (born 1968) is a sinologist and historian. She studied at Pearson College London, the Mandarin Training Center, the University of Oxford, and Heidelberg University, where she took up a post in 1993.

Barbara Nimri Aziz (born 1940) is a Tibetology and religious studies scholar. She completed a B.A. at Queen's University at Kingston and earned a Ph.D. under Christoph von Fürer-Haimendorf at SOAS in 1974, later holding a post at the University of Oran (2007).

Barbara Stoler Miller (1940–1993) was an Indologist. Educated at Barnard College, Columbia University, and the University of Pennsylvania (Ph.D. under W. Norman Brown and Stella Kramrisch), she served on the faculties of Barnard College (1968–1979) and Columbia University (~1968–1993).

Barbra R. Clayton is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She completed her Ph.D. at McGill University under Richard P. Hayes and Katherine K. Young, and held a post at Mount Allison University (attested 2013).
Barend Faddegon (1874–1955) was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied at the University of Amsterdam from circa 1898 to 1906 and later served on its faculty from 1907 to 1944.

Barend J. ter Haar (born 1958) is a sinologist and historian. He earned his PhD at Leiden University under Erik Zürcher and held academic positions at Heidelberg University (~1994–2000), Leiden University (~2000–2013), and the University of Hamburg (~2018).

Barend Jan Terwiel (born 1941) is a historian and scholar of Buddhism and religion. Educated at Utrecht University and the Australian National University (Ph.D.), he held positions at ANU, the University of Munich, Leiden University, and the University of Hamburg (1992–2007).

Barnabás Csongor (1923–2018) was a sinologist and linguist. He studied at Budapest University of Technology and Economics and Eötvös Loránd University, where he later taught from circa 1950 to 1993, alongside holding a post at Princeton University.
